questions.question: What does the SQ3R reading method stand for?
questions.explanation: SQ3R is a structured reading method: Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.

questions.question: What should an active reader do BEFORE reading a non-fiction text?
options: Preview the text, set a purpose and activate prior knowledge
Read the whole text twice quickly
questions.explanation: The before-phase includes previewing, setting a purpose for reading and activating what you already know.

questions.question: What does annotating a text involve?
options: Marking key points and writing notes while reading
questions.explanation: Annotation — underlining key points and writing margin notes — is a core during-reading strategy.

questions.question: Why is recognising text structure useful when reading non-fiction?
options: Structures like cause-effect and compare-contrast help you predict and organise information
It tells you whether the text is true
questions.explanation: Recognising structures (cause-effect, problem-solution, compare-contrast) helps you follow and remember the content.

questions.question: What should you do AFTER reading a non-fiction text?
options: Summarise, evaluate and connect the content to what you know
questions.explanation: The after-phase consolidates understanding: summarise the content, evaluate it and connect it to prior knowledge.
